title: Bluesky Is Blocking Links to a Major Leak of DHS Employee Records
gist: Bluesky is blocking links to the DDoSecrets 'Icepick' DHS leak and its search site as 'malicious', citing guidelines against sharing personal contact info, while X's Grok pointed users to the archive; the episode highlights platform moderation conflict over government transparency.

insights.claim: Bluesky blocked links to the DHS archive and crimew's search site, labeling them 'malicious', and says it chose link blocking over removing individual posts to avoid limiting discussion.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Link-level blocking is a moderation choice that invites criticism on neutrality.
insights.locator: Bluesky is blocking users from opening links

insights.claim: Bluesky did not say whether the block was automatic or requested by a government agency, and the DDoSecrets homepage still loads and at least one third-party app (Klearsky) opens the archive without warning.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Open protocol lets third-party apps diverge from first-party moderation.

insights.claim: Bluesky guidelines bar sharing contact info but protect factual reporting on government transparency, creating tension since the leak content is largely business-card-level data.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Policy ambiguity is a trust-and-safety risk for the platform.
insights.locator: Its current community guidelines bar sharing

insights.claim: Bluesky reached 45 million registered accounts by August and about 10.4 million mobile users in June, and is run by Toni Schneider after Jay Graber stepped down in March.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Sizes the platform whose moderation precedent is being set.
insights.locator: By August of this year, it counted 45 million

insights.claim: On X, the Grok chatbot pointed users to the Icepick site and described how to download the dataset, a contrast with Bluesky's approach.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: AI chatbots become unmoderated distribution channels for leaked data.

insights.claim: DDoSecrets' Emma Best says platforms often give in to government pressure, citing Twitter's 2020 suspension and blocking after the BlueLeaks release, but 'can't stop the signal'.
insights.speaker: Dhruv Mehrotra
insights.so_what: Platform blocking has historically had limited effect on spread.
